options: Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct.
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct.
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are incorrect.
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect.
81748.sol: The reaction of NaCl with concentrated H ₂ SO ₄ and MnO ₂ is given by: 2 NaCl + MnO ₂ + 2 H ₂ SO ₄ Na ₂ SO ₄ + MnSO ₄ + 2 H ₂ O + Cl ₂ In this reaction, the oxidation state of Mn changes from +4 in MnO ₂ to +2 in MnSO ₄ . Since the oxidation state decreases, Mn undergoes reduction, not oxidation. Thus, Statement-I is incorrect. The reaction of NaI with concentrated H ₂ SO ₄ and MnO ₂ is given by: 2 NaI + MnO ₂ + 2 H ₂ SO ₄ Na ₂ SO ₄ + MnSO ₄ + 2 H ₂ O + I ₂ Here, the oxidation state of Mn also changes from +4 to +2

85558.subject: Zoology
85558.text: Presence of gills in the tadpole of frog indicates that:

85558.sol: Tadpoles are the larval forms of frog and toads. They respire through gills whereas the adult form respire through the skin and lungs. Since, fishes also respires through gills. Hence, presence of gills in the tadpole indicates that frogs are evolved from gilled ancestors. Related Theory "Ontogeny recapitulates phylogeny" mean that the development of individual organisms (ontogeny) follows (recapitulates) the same phases of the evolution of larger ancestral groups of related organisms (phylogeny).

100493.subject: Physics
100493.text: A car is negotiating a flat, unbanked circular turn. For a turn of radius R , the maximum safe speed of the car without skidding is v . If the radius of the turn is increased to 4R while the coefficient of static friction remains the same, what will be the new maximum safe speed for the car?
100493.sol: The maximum safe speed for a car on a flat circular track is determined by the static friction providing the necessary centripetal force. Equating the maximum static friction to the required centripetal force: mv^2 R = mg Solving for v , we get: v = R g This shows that the maximum safe speed is directly proportional to the square root of the radius of the turn ( v R ). When the radius is increased to 4R , the new maximum safe speed v' is: v' = (4R) g = 2 R g = 2v . Answer: 2v

105280.text: An unregulated DC power supply of 12 V is connected across a series combination of a resistor of 1 k and a Zener diode. The Zener diode has a breakdown voltage of 5 V and is connected in reverse bias. Assuming no load resistor is connected across the Zener diode, what is the current flowing through the series resistor?
105280.sol: The Zener diode is connected in reverse bias and the input voltage ( 12 V ) is greater than the Zener breakdown voltage ( 5 V ). Therefore, the Zener diode operates in the breakdown region and maintains a constant voltage of 5 V across itself. The voltage drop across the series resistor is the difference between the input voltage and the Zener voltage: V_R = V_ in - V_Z = 12 V - 5 V = 7 V Using Ohm's law, the current flowing through the series resistor is: I = V_R R = 7 V 1 k = 7 mA Answer: 7 mA

If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion
If assertion is true, but reason is false
Both assertion and reason are false statements.

Also photorespiration is negligible or absent in these plants. So, they are photosynthetically more efficient than C ₃ plants. These plants show a special type of leaf anatomy called Kranz anatomy. 126366.subject: Botany
126366.text: When pollen tube enters through micropyle, the process is called
126366.sol: The pollen tube may enter the ovule by following one of three routes given below: (1) Porogamy Pollen tube enters the ovule through micropyle, e.g., most angiosperms. (2) Mesogamy Pollen tube enters the ovule through integuments (e.g., Cucurbita) or through funiculus (e.g., Pistacia). (3) Chalazogamy Pollen tube enters the ovule through chalazal tissues, e.g., Casuarina, Beta vulgaris, Juglens regia, etc.

126489.subject: Botany
126489.text: What is the pitch of B-DNA?
126489.sol: There are two hydrogen bonds between A and T in DNA and 3 between G and C. One full turn of the helical strand in DNA involves ten base pairs or ten steps of ascent. Each step of ascent measures 3.4Å. Hence, the pitch of B-DNA is 34Å. The rise per base pair in B-DNA is 3.4Å.

126704.sol: The exoskeleton of arthropods is made of a complex polysaccharide called chitin. Chitin is a nitrogen-containing polysaccharide composed of N-acetyl glucosamine monomers. According to NCERT, complex polysaccharides like chitin are mostly homopolymers, meaning they are built from the repetition of a single type of monomeric unit. 126834.subject: Botany

127411.subject: Botany
127411.text: A conservationist aims to preserve the gametes of a highly endangered animal species in a viable and fertile condition for a long period of time. Identify the appropriate technique for this purpose and the category of biodiversity conservation it represents.
127411.sol: According to NCERT, in recent years, ex-situ conservation has advanced beyond keeping threatened species in enclosures. The gametes of threatened species can now be preserved in viable and fertile conditions for long periods using cryopreservation techniques (preservation at ultra-low temperatures, typically -196^ C in liquid nitrogen). 127624.subject: Botany
127624.text: What is the shape of the pyramid of number, biomass and energy in most ecosystems?
127624.sol: Any calculations of energy content, biomass or numbers, has to include all organisms at that trophic level. No generalisations we make will be true if we take only a few individuals at any trophic level into account. Also a given organism may occupy more than one trophic level simultaneously. One must remember that the trophic level represents a functional level, not a species as such. A given species may occupy more than one trophic level in the same ecosystem at the same time; for example, a sparrow is a primary

127873.subject: Zoology
127873.text: What is the composition of the body of a simple organism like Hydra?
127873.sol: In the preceding chapters you came across a large variety of organisms, both unicellular and multicellular, of the animal kingdom. In unicellular organisms, all functions like digestion, respiration and reproduction are performed by a single cell. In the complex body of multicellular animals the same basic functions are carried out by different groups of cells in a well organised manner. The body of a simple organism like Hydra is made of different types of cells and the number of cells in each type can be in thous

127995.subject: Zoology
127995.text: Where are the ovaries situated in female frogs?
127995.sol: Frogs have well organised male and female reproductive systems. Male reproductive organs consist of a pair of yellowish ovoid testes , which are found adhered to the upper part of kidneys by a double fold of peritoneum called mesorchium. Vasa efferentia are 10-12 in number that arise from testes. They enter the kidneys on their side and open into Bidder’s canal. Finally it communicates with the urinogenital duct that comes out of the kidneys and opens into the cloaca. The cloaca is a small, median chamber that is u

128380.subject: Zoology
128380.text: What are the two groups of steroid hormones produced by the ovary?
128380.sol: Females have a pair of ovaries located in the abdomen (Figure 19.1). Ovary is the primary female sex organ which produces one ovum during each menstrual cycle. In addition, ovary also produces two groups of steroid hormones called estrogen and progesterone. Ovary is composed of ovarian follicles and stromal tissues. The estrogen is synthesised and secreted mainly by the growing ovarian follicles. After ovulation, the ruptured follicle is converted to a structure called corpus luteum, which secretes mainly progester

128518.text: Read the following statements and choose the correct option: 1. Small amounts of androgenic steroids are also secreted by the adrenal cortex during puberty 2. Pancreas is a composite gland which acts as both exocrine and endocrine gland 3. Testis functions only as an endocrine gland 4. Androgens influence male libido
128518.sol: Small amounts of androgenic steroids are also secreted by the adrenal cortex during puberty. Pancreas is a composite gland which acts as both exocrine and endocrine gland

128558.subject: Zoology
128558.text: What is the target gland of Thyrotrophin hormone?
128558.sol: The target gland of thyrotropin hormone is thyroid gland

128763.subject: Zoology
128763.text: How do simple organisms like sponges and coelenterates circulate substances within their bodies?
128763.sol: Different groups of animals have evolved different methods for this transport. Simple organisms like sponges and coelenterates circulate water from their surroundings through their body cavities to facilitate the cells to exchange these substances . More complex organisms use special fluids within their bodies to transport such materials. Blood is the most commonly used body fluid by most of the higher organisms including humans for this purpose.

128983.subject: Zoology
128983.text: ECG Wave Cardiac Event A. P wave 1. Ventricular repolarization B. QRS complex 2. Atrial depolarization C. T wave 3. Ventricular depolarization D. U wave 4. Recovery of Purkinje fibers
128983.sol: The P wave represents atrial depolarization. The QRS complex represents ventricular depolarization. The T wave represents ventricular repolarization. The U wave represents the recovery of Purkinje fibers.

129027.subject: Zoology

129027.sol: Plasma is viscous and straw-coloured fluid.

129242.subject: Zoology

129242.sol: A deep cleft divides the cerebrum longitudinally into two halves, which are called the left and right cerebral hemispheres. The cerebral cortex contains motor areas, sensory areas, and large regions that are neither clearly sensory nor motor in function. These regions, called the association areas, are responsible for complex functions such as intersensory associations, memory and communication. The association areas in the brain are responsible for complex functions such as intersensory associations, memory and co

129420.text: Pneumotoxic centre which can moderate the functions of the respiratory rhythm centre is present at
129420.sol: Pneumotoxic centre which can moderate the functions of the respiratory rhythm centre is present in the pons region of the brain. Neural signals from this centre can reduce the duration of inspiration and there by alter the respiration rate.

129440.subject: Zoology
129440.text: Parkinson's disease (characterized by tremors and progressive rigidity of limbs) is caused by degeneration of brain neurons that are involved in movement control and make use of neurotransmitter
129440.sol: Deficiency of dopamine in the human produces symptoms of Parkinson's disease.

129543.subject: Zoology
129543.text: Which segment of the renal system allows the passage of small amounts of urea?
129543.sol: NaCl is transported by the ascending limb of Henle’s loop which is exchanged with the descending limb of vasa recta. NaCl is returned to the interstitium by the ascending portion of vasa recta. Similarly, small amounts of urea enter the thin segment of the ascending limb of Henle’s loop which is transported back to the interstitium by the collecting tubule. The above described transport of substances facilitated by the special arrangement of Henle’s loop and vasa recta is called the counter current mechanism.

129644.subject: Zoology

129644.sol: Earthworms use nephridia for excretion. Flatworms use flame cells. Insects use Malpighian tubules. Vertebrates use kidneys

129741.subject: Zoology
129741.text: Which of the following waste products in grasshopper is not excreted and is used in other metabolic activities?
129741.sol: Excretory organs of grasshopper are the Malpighian tubules and the main excretory product is uric acid. Malpighian tubules of insects such as grasshoppers not only help to excrete the waste but also function to conserve water, which is then used in other metabolic activities. In the Malpighian tubules, bicarbonates of potassium and sodium, water and uric acid are formed during the process of excretion. A large amount of water and bicarbonates of potassium and sodium are reabsorbed by the cells of Malpighian tubules

129851.subject: Zoology
129851.text: What are Alveoli in the respiratory system?

Sites for exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide
Structures involved in the production of mucus
Centers for processing of air inhaled
129851.sol: Alveoli are the primary sites of exchange of gases. Exchange of gases also occur between blood and tissues. O2 and CO2 are exchanged in these sites by simple diffusion mainly based on pressure/concentration gradient . Solubility of the gases as well as the thickness of the membranes involved in diffusion are also some important factors that can affect the rate of diffusion. 129884.text: What happens to oxygen when it reaches the tissues?

This curve is called the Oxygen dissociation curve and is highly useful in studying the effect of factors like pCO2, H+ concentration, etc., on binding of O2 with haemoglobin. 130031.text: During a normal respiration, the volume of air expired or inspired is referred to as ___ volume.
130031.sol: During a normal respiration, the volume of air expired or inspired is referred to as tidal volume.

130749.subject: Zoology
130749.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): Surgical methods of contraception are highly effective but their reversibility is very poor. Reason (R): Surgical intervention blocks gamete transport and thereby prevents conception. 130876.subject: Zoology
130876.text: What is the result of the second meiotic division of the secondary spermatocytes?
options: Formation of two equal, haploid spermatids
Formation of four equal, haploid spermatozoa
Formation of two equal, diploid primary spermatocytes
Formation of two unequal, haploid spermatids
130876.sol: Some of the spermatogonia called primary spermatocytes periodically undergo meiosis. A primary spermatocyte completes the first meiotic division (reduction division) leading to formation of two equal, haploid cells called secondary spermatocytes, which have only 23 chromosomes each. The secondary spermatocytes undergo the second meiotic division to produce four equal, haploid spermatids. 131500.sol: The DNA polymerases on their own cannot initiate the process of replication. Also the replication does not initiate randomly at any place in DNA. options: To bind to specific amino acids
131551.sol: From the very beginning of the proposition of code, it was clear to Francis Crick that there has to be a mechanism to read the code and also to link it to the amino acids, because amino acids have no structural specialities to read the code uniquely. He postulated the presence of an adapter molecule that would on one hand read the code and on other hand would bind to specific amino acids. The tRNA, then called sRNA (soluble RNA), was known before the genetic code was postulated. However, its role as an adapter mole

options: They are involved in different metabolic pathways
They code for proteins that are needed together to function in the same or related metabolic pathways
They are not involved in any metabolic pathways
131583.sol: The lac operon consists of one regulatory gene (the i gene – here the term i does not refer to inducer, rather it is derived from the word inhibitor) and three structural genes (z, y, and a). The i gene codes for the repressor of the lac operon. The z gene codes for beta-galactosidase (β-gal), which is primarily responsible for the hydrolysis of the disaccharide, lactose into its monomeric units, galactose and glucose. 131607.subject: Zoology

These repetitive DNA are separated from bulk genomic DNA as different peaks during density gradient centrifugation. The bulk DNA forms a major peak and the other small peaks are referred to as satellite DNA. Depending on base composition (A : T rich or G:C rich), length of segment, and number of repetitive units, the satellite

This antibiotic was extensively used to treat American soldiers wounded in World War II. Fleming, Chain

133791.subject: Zoology
133791.text: How does the organic farmer approach controlling pests?
options: By keeping insects at manageable levels through a complex system of checks and balances within a living and vi
By ignoring the presence of pests
133791.sol: In agriculture, there is a method of controlling pests that relies on natural predation rather than introduced chemicals. A key belief of the organic farmer is that biodiversity furthers health. The more variety a landscape has, the more sustainable it is. The organic farmer, therefore, works to create a system where the insects that are sometimes called pests are not eradicated, but instead are kept at manageable levels by a complex system of checks and balances within a living and vibrant ecosystem.

134693.sol: When cut by the same restriction enzyme, the resultant DNA fragments have the same kind of ‘sticky-ends’ and, these can be joined together (end-to-end) using DNA ligases.

135457.subject: Zoology
135457.text: The growth curve of bacterial population in lab is plotted against time. What will be the shape of graph?
135457.sol: Under continuous supply of food and space in the laboratory conditions the bacterial population grows exponentially and shows a Jshaped curve, thus the curve would be hyperbolic. Such populations ultimately crash when the population size grows beyond carrying capacity.

6a0e2779165ae1327797b3d7.sol: Members of the class Chondrichthyes (cartilaginous fishes) lack an air bladder (swim bladder), which is a buoyancy-regulating organ found in osteichthyes (bony fishes). 6a104ff88b46719ce7976ce8.subject: Physics

95636.subject: Botany
options: Cyanobacteria form mycorrhizae which helps in the absorption of phosphate
Salvinia, Selaginella and Azolla show heterospory.
The genome of TMV is RNA.
95636.sol: "Myco" - "rhiza" literally means "fungus" - "root" and describes the mutually beneficial relationship between the plant and root fungus. These specialized fungi colonize plant roots in a symbiotic manner and extend far into the soil. Mycorrhizal fungal filaments in the soil are truly extensions of root systems and are more effective in nutrient and water absorption than the roots themselves. Cyanobacteria on the other hand is not a fungus.

95654.subject: Botany
95654.text: Select the option having the fungi which belong to the same class
95654.sol: Rhizopus and Mucor are members of Phycomycetes. Aspergillus , Saccharomyces (yeast), Morchella (morels) are Ascomycetes fungi. Agaricus (Mushroom) contains edible Basidiomycetes fungi. Morchella , commonly called as morels, are edible Ascomycetes fungi.

95859.subject: Botany
95859.text: The characteristic pigment of Cyanobacteria is
95859.sol: Cyanobacteria are a group of free-living photosynthetic bacteria that perform oxygenic photosynthetic process which are included in the kingdom Monera. It contains the main green pigment chlorophyll a for photosynthesis as this group have both the photosystems -PS I and PS II. Phycobilins are also present that gives the blue colour.

96001.subject: Botany
96001.text: Which of the following organelles is bound by the tonoplast?
96001.sol: The vacuole is the membrane-bound space found in the cytoplasm. It contains water, sap, excretory product and other materials not useful for the cell. The vacuole is bound by a single membrane called tonoplast.

96072.subject: Botany
96072.text: Which of the following organelles is present exclusively in plants?
96072.sol: The glyoxysome was discovered by Beevers and Breidenbach in 1961. These are specialized peroxisomes that are found only in plants(germinating seeds). They also possess the key enzyme for the glyoxylate cycle. They contain an enzyme that initiates the breakdown of fatty acids and also helps in the synthesis of sugar by gluconeogenesis.

96082.subject: Botany

96082.sol: The endomembrane system include endoplasmic reticulum (ER), golgi complex, lysosomes and vacuoles. Since the functions of the mitochondria, chloroplast and peroxisomes are not coordinated with the above components, these are not considered as part of the endomembrane system. Mitochondria are the sites of aerobic respiration. They produce cellular energy in the form of ATP, hence they are called ‘power houses’ of the cell. 96989.sol: Fabaceae, i.e. Leguminosae is the family of plant having legumes, peas group in them. This group is the third largest group and economically important family of flowering plants. In this group the following floral characteristics are observed. The flower is bisexual and zygomorphic with superior ovary and diadelphous anther. 97116.subject: Botany
97116.text: The correct meaning of the expression 'gynoecium is apocarpous' is
options: gynoecium comprises only one pistil which is fused with stamens
gynoecium comprises more than one carpel, all of which are free.
gynoecium comprises more than one carpel, which are fused.
gynoecium comprises only one carpel, which is free.
97116.sol: The gynoecium is the female reproductive part of flower and its unit is carpel or pistil. If gynoecium carpel may be single (monocarpellary) or several (multicarpellary). In multicarpellary condition, carpels may be free (apocarpous) or fused (syncarpous). Apocarpous gynoecium can be seen in lotus, rose, etc., while syncarpous gynoecium can be seen in mustard, tomato, etc.

97256.subject: Botany
97256.text: Which of the following is not the function of auxins?
97256.sol: Auxins help to initiate rooting in stem cuttings, an application widely used for plant propagation. Auxins promote flowering e.g. in pineapples. They help to prevent fruit and leaf drop at early stages but promote the abscission of older mature leaves and fruits. In most higher plants, the growing apical bud inhibits the growth of the lateral (axillary) buds, a phenomenon called apical dominance. Auxins also induce parthenocarpy, e.g., in tomatoes. They are widely used as herbicides. 2, 4-D, widely used to kill dic

97571.subject: Botany
97571.text: A small protein that is attached to the outer surface of the inner membrane of mitochondria and acts as a mobile carrier for electron transfer in oxidative phosphorylation is
options: Ubiquinone that receives electron from complex I only
Cytochrome c 1 between complex III and complex IV
Cytochrome c between complex III and complex IV
97571.sol: The metabolic pathway through which the electron passes from one carrier to another, is called the electron transport system (ETS). This pathway is present in the inner mitochondrial membrane. Electrons from NADH (produced in the mitochondria matrix) are oxidized by an NADH dehydrogenase (Complex I) and are transferred to ubiquinone (Complex II). The reduced ubiquinone (ubiquinol) is then oxidised with the transfer of electrons to cytochrome c via cytochrome bc1 complex (complex III). Cytochrome c is a small protei

97592.subject: Botany
97592.text: In which one of the following, do both the names refer to the same thing?
options: Tricarboxylic acid cycle and urea cycle
Tricarboxylic acid cycle and citric acid cycle
Citric acid cycle and Calvin cycle
97592.sol: The TCA cycle is also called the citric acid cycle because the first stable product formed is a tricarboxylic acid molecule that is citric acid. Hence the name citric acid cycle. It is also called the Kreb's cycle.
